_doc: POST-OPENER INTENTS - the operator's recurring follow-up asks, declared as data (the registry half of the stop governor; the drift predicate is scripts/check-stop-governor.py, the executable half is scripts/stop-governor.py).

intents: one row per family of the study's section 3 table (docs/prompt-control-vocabulary-study.md), with the study's n. The predicate holds the ids and counts in parity with that table, so a re-counted study is a red check, not a memory chore.

rules: the executable behaviors. A rule fires at the turn-end boundary and emits ONE bounded continuation written in the operator's own lowercase lexicon. Every rule ships in mode shadow: it logs would_block and changes nothing. mode live needs a promotion block, and the predicate refuses a live rule without one. That is a DECLARED-EVIDENCE gate, not a verified one: replay/shadow numbers are self-attested (the predicate requires them, a tracked receipt path that exists, and the precision floor, but cannot recompute them until stop-governor-measure.py exists); an operator promotion must cite a GitHub issue or pull-request URL.

Hooks cannot type a slash command (Claude hooks docs), so a rule fires the PROMPT BODY the command would carry. Names come from the operator's lexicon: each rule's text must contain one of its own lexicon phrases, and each phrase must appear verbatim in the study.
Nothing here arms a settings file. Arming is one paste, staged at docs/keys/stop-governor-settings-snippet.json and filed as lever L-STOP-GOVERNOR-ARM.
gate_clause: if a step sends, deletes, spends or leaks: say BLOCKED: <atom> once and stop.
status_suffix: end w: merged / live / observed / left · tldr · what you need to do: none or the one atom.

_doc: Detection vocabulary for scripts/stop-governor.py. Phrase lists match whole words, case-insensitively; *_patterns are regex fragments anchored at a word start and a word end.

permission_questions fire CONT only when the message ENDS in a question mark; handbacks (menus, 'run this yourself') need none. Offers such as 'let me know if' and 'you can run' are deliberately absent: they appear on ordinary completion messages where nothing is pending.

deny_patterns gate CONT only, the one rule that pushes new work. They are a BEST-EFFORT lexical filter, not a guarantee: the litmus is destroying, sending, spending or irreversibly leaking, plus the production guardrail, and the gate clause in every continuation (BLOCKED: <atom> once) is the backstop behind them. A new outward verb found in shadow samples is added here before any promotion. Roots are written to catch inflections that drop a final e (delet-, remov-, wip-). Shipment steps (commit, push) are standing grants and are not here; 'merge' is, because the MERGE rule and scripts/merge-policy.sh own that decision.
negation, failure_terms and hold_patterns keep a completion claim, exit evidence and a merge ask honest: 'not done', '3 passed, 2 failed' and 'do not merge yet' do not count.

CONT.text: proceed w ur suggestion--you do it. take the reversible best option and fix all inside this ask; dont ask again. anything past the ask goes on a next: line, not done.

lexicon: were all of the findings healed and addressed?
VERIFY.text: were all of the findings healed and addressed? run scripts/verify-scoped.sh bare on this exact tree and read its own exit code. anything strange? heal it root-to-leaf.

CLOSE.text: closeout means closeout, nothing hanging: .agents/skills/closeout/SKILL.md steps 4-7. session release, task completion, estate health and deletion eligibility are distinct claims--report an inherited red on its own estate: line. print the terminal line only on a bare exit 0. safe to archive session? say yes or no w the evidence.

lexicon: merge it if the baseline passes
MERGE.text: merge it if the baseline passes: read logs/AUTONOMY_PAUSED first, run scripts/merge-policy.sh <pr> and follow the printed MERGE-MODE and MERGE-HEAD once. on exit 2 or 3 say the verdict once and stop. no waiting, no polling.

lexicon: whats next ostensibly and extensibly alpha to omega/root to leaf re:this-workstream?
NEXT.text: whats next ostensibly and extensibly alpha to omega/root to leaf re:this-workstream? say the ideal-form next step on a next: line; if its reversible and inside the ask, do it.

lexicon: what do i need to do
status update--what's merged and what's left?
STATUS.text: tldr and eli5--status update--what's merged and what's left? give percent complete. what do i need to do? answer on one line: what you need to do: none or the one atom.

HARNESS.owner: harness built-ins (/compact /model /effort /voice /loop /goal); no hook can run a built-in. The governor yields to /loop (session_crons) and to any active continuation.

SHELL.owner: Hypothesis, not established by the study (it lists only phrasings such as !gh pr merge and !chezmoi apply): typed shell is the operator doing what a permission prompt blocked. Related owners: lever L-AGENT-BASH-PROMPT (the trust hook scripts/hooks/allow-trusted-cd-git.sh) and the Codex action admission.

CORRECT.owner: AGENTS.md Standing Corrections and the existing PreToolUse guards; the detectable families (handed-back work, permission-seeking, claim without evidence, inherited-red closeout) are covered by the CONT, VERIFY and CLOSE rules. The CORRECT rate after arming is the governor's misfire signal.
CORRECT.claude_binding: via the CONT, VERIFY and CLOSE rules
CORRECT.codex_binding: via the CONT, VERIFY and CLOSE rules
CORRECT.evidence: study sections 3 and 5: 9 of 15 correction families restate a written rule (section 5 counts about 122 correction turns, section 3 counts 140; unreconciled)
